served.stem: Filtration of plasma from the glomerular capillaries into Bowman's capsule is driven mainly by which of the following?
choices: Colloid osmotic pressure of the plasma proteins
served.bankWhy: Filtration here is a plumbing question rather than a transport question. Blood enters the glomerulus through a wide afferent arteriole and leaves through a narrower efferent one, which holds capillary hydrostatic pressure high and pushes water and small solutes through the filtration barrier in bulk. Net filtration is that pushing pressure minus the opposing plasma colloid osmotic pressure and capsular pressure, so the choice naming hydrostatic pressure is the driving force.

choiceTexts: Colloid osmotic pressure of the plasma proteins

answer.line: Blood pressure in the glomerular capillaries pushes water and small solutes into the capsule. It is bulk flow, and it costs no ATP.

steps: Name the forces at the glomerulus. Blood pressure pushes fluid out, while plasma proteins pull it back and capsule fluid pushes back.
Look at the plumbing. A wide afferent arteriole in and a narrow efferent one out hold that blood pressure high.
So the push wins. Net filtration is hydrostatic pressure minus the two opposing forces.

choices.text: Colloid osmotic pressure of the plasma proteins
choices.note: The plasma proteins stay in the capillary, and their osmotic pull draws fluid back in. It works against filtration, not for it.
Active transport does its work later, when the tubule reabsorbs. Filtration itself spends no ATP.
The aquaporins ADH controls sit in the collecting duct, far downstream. Nothing called an aquaporin gradient drives filtration.
Capillary blood pressure drives bulk flow into the capsule.
Diffusion moves each solute down its own gradient, as in gas exchange. Filtration pushes water and small solutes through together, in bulk.

student.lockIt: Filtration is pressure: blood pressure pushes out, plasma proteins pull back, and the push wins.
